title: Mapping-simplex quasi-equivalences are categorical equivalences after arbitrary base change
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cartesian fibrations and cartesian edges from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], categorical equivalences from [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], and the marked mapping simplex $M^m(A)$ from [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation]. Let $n\geq0$, let $p:Y\to\Delta^n$ be a cartesian fibration with $Y$ small, and let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ be a chain of small simplicial sets. Suppose $q:M^m(A)\to Y$ is a simplicial map over $\Delta^n$, takes every edge $(\alpha,a)$ with $a$ degenerate to a $p$-cartesian edge, and induces a categorical equivalence $A_i\to Y\times_{\Delta^n}\{i\}$ for each $0\leq i\leq n$. For every small simplicial set $T$ and every simplicial map $t:T\to\Delta^n$, the induced map of underlying simplicial sets
$$q_T:M^m(A)\times_{\Delta^n}T\longrightarrow Y\times_{\Delta^n}T$$
is a categorical equivalence. Neither $T$ nor the $A_i$ are required to be quasicategories, and $t$ need not be injective. Empty simplicial sets and $n=0$ are included.

source.place: Definition 3.2.2.6 and Proposition 3.2.2.7(2), printed pp. 180-181 (PDF pp. 198-199); proof via Proposition 3.2.2.8 and Proposition 3.2.2.10. Read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result; archival HTT copy WANTED.

proof.text:
Fix $r>0$, an inner fibration $p:Z\to\Delta^r$ of quasicategories, a $p$-Cartesian edge $e:b\to c$ over $r-1\to r$, and a vertex $a$ with $p(a)\leq r-1$. By [lem-cbc-coherent-cartesian-postcomposition], applied to $E=Z$, $B=\Delta^r$ and this $p,e,a$, the strictly commutative square of enriched mapping simplicial sets with top row $[e]\circ-:\mathfrak C[Z](a,b)\to\mathfrak C[Z](a,c)$, vertical maps induced by $\mathfrak C[p]$, and bottom row
$$\mathfrak C[\Delta^r](p(a),r-1)\xrightarrow{[p(e)]\circ-}\mathfrak C[\Delta^r](p(a),r)$$
is a homotopy pullback square. Since $p(a)\leq r-1<r$, both bottom objects are weakly contractible and the bottom arrow is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-standard-simplex-mapping-contractible]. After the functorial Kan replacement in the definition of homotopy pullback, the path-space fiber product of the other three corners projects to the replaced upper right corner by the base change of the path-space factorization of the bottom arrow, a trivial Kan fibration; pullbacks of trivial fibrations are trivial fibrations. Hence the top arrow $\mathfrak C[Z](a,b)\to\mathfrak C[Z](a,c)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is the postcomposition assertion used in step 4; it makes no Kan assertion about the unreplaced enriched mapping sets.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, (1)$\Rightarrow$(2), read in the coherent-realization model of its own remark (printed pp. 131-132); Definition 1.1.5.1; the sentence of the proof of Proposition 3.2.2.10 (printed p. 184) that the bottom horizontal arrow is a weak homotopy equivalence because $q(e)$ is $p$-Cartesian.

proof.text: Use the simplex, operator, marking and vertex-fiber construction clauses of [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation]. We prove by induction on $r\geq0$ that every map satisfying the hypotheses over $\Delta^r$ is a categorical equivalence, without yet making arbitrary base changes. For $r=0$ the mapping simplex is $A_0$ and the map is the assumed fibre equivalence. For $r>0$ put $H=\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,r-1\}}$, $Y_-=Y\times_{\Delta^r}H$, $Y_+=Y_r$, $M_-=M(A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_{r-1})$ and $M_+=A_r$. Restricting $q$ gives maps $q_-:M_-\to Y_-$ and $q_+:A_r\to Y_r$. The map $Y_-\to H$ is a cartesian fibration: each horn problem projects to one for $p$ with the prescribed simplex of $H$, and its filler pairs with that simplex; a cartesian lift of an edge of $H$ also pairs with that edge, and its last-horn fillers pair in the same way. Its total simplicial set is a quasicategory, since an inner horn projects to one in $H$, is filled there, and then lifts through the inner fibration. The restriction $q_-$ preserves the specified marked edges and has exactly the original fibre maps. Thus the induction hypothesis applies to $q_-$; the hypothesis at $r$ applies to $q_+$.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.10, induction and initial-face restriction; elementary horn-pullback verification.

proof.text: Put $C=\mathfrak C[M]$, $D=\mathfrak C[Y]$ and $F=\mathfrak C[q]$. The full enriched subcategories on vertices over $0,\ldots,r-1$ are exactly $\mathfrak C[M_-]$ and $\mathfrak C[Y_-]$, and those on vertices over $r$ are $\mathfrak C[A_r]$ and $\mathfrak C[Y_r]$. To check fullness from the coherent-realization definition, a generator from vertices $i$ to $j$ of a simplex uses only the subinterval $[i,j]$ and its subsets. Projecting that interval to $[r]$ is monotone. If its endpoints lie in the initial face, that whole interval lies there; if both project to $r$, it lies in the final fibre. A composite word cannot leave either region and return, and the simplex face/degeneracy and union relations restrict to the same relations in that region. There are no generators or words going from the final region to the initial one. Hence both $C,D$ have empty mapping sets in that direction. By [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection], the categorical equivalences $q_-,q_+$ from step 2 give Dwyer--Kan equivalences on these two full enriched subcategories. Thus $F$ induces weak homotopy equivalences on all same-region mapping sets and is essentially surjective on each region. The only mapping sets not yet checked go from an initial-region vertex to a final-region vertex.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.10, the decomposition into initial and final full enriched subcategories; explicit generator argument for fullness.

proof.text: Let $x\in C_-$ and $y\in C_+$, and regard $y$ as a vertex of $A_r$. Let $y'\in A_{r-1}$ be its image and $e:y'\to y$ the marked edge with second coordinate $s_0y$. The enriched functor $F$ gives a strictly commuting square whose top and bottom maps are respectively $[e]\circ-:C(x,y')\to C(x,y)$ and $[q(e)]\circ-:D(Fx,Fy')\to D(Fx,Fy)$, and whose vertical maps are those induced by $F$ on the indicated mapping sets. The left vertical map is a weak homotopy equivalence by step 3. The top map is a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-mapping-simplex-final-edge], since $x$ lies before the final fibre; its statement allows arbitrary simplicial sets $A_i$. The edge $q(e)$ is $p$-cartesian by the assumption that $q$ carries every marked edge to a $p$-cartesian edge and $p(qx)\leq r-1$, so the bottom map is a weak homotopy equivalence by step 1. The two composites around the square agree, so their bijections on components and isomorphisms on all based homotopy groups make the right vertical map a weak homotopy equivalence as well.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.10, mixed mapping-set square, using Lemma 3.2.2.9; source printed p. 184 (PDF page 202).

proof.text: Every object of $D$ belongs to one of its two regions. The essential surjectivity of the restricted functors in step 3 therefore supplies, for every object of $D$, an isomorphism in $\pi_0D$ to some $F$-image. All mapping sets are weakly equivalent under $F$: the same-region cases were checked in step 3, the forward mixed cases in step 4, and the reverse mixed cases are the identity of empty simplicial sets. This is precisely a Dwyer--Kan equivalence as defined in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. By [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection], $q$ is a categorical equivalence. This completes the dimension induction, using no assertion about arbitrary pullbacks during that induction.

source.place: Conclusion of Proposition 3.2.2.10, detection by coherent realization.

proof.text: Use the same construction clauses of [lem-coef-cartesian-mapping-simplex-presentation]. For an arbitrary simplex $\sigma:\Delta^r\to\Delta^n$, write its monotone vertex map as $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$. The pullback $M(A)\times_{\Delta^n}\Delta^r$ is the mapping simplex for $B_j=A_{\alpha(j)}$, with transition the composite original transition; repeated values of $\alpha$ give identity transitions. Indeed its $k$-simplices are exactly $(\beta,a)$ with $\beta:[k]\to[r]$ and $a\in(A_{\alpha\beta(k)})_k$, and its operators are exactly the original restriction followed by the indicated chain transition. This is an isomorphism in every degree, commuting with all operators. The specified marked edges remain the edges with degenerate second coordinate. The pullback $Y_\sigma\to\Delta^r$ is a cartesian fibration by the horn-and-pairing argument in step 2, including cartesian lifts and quasicategory total space. A marked edge maps to the pair of the original $p$-cartesian edge and its specified base edge; its last-horn lifts again pair, so it is cartesian in the pullback. Its fibre maps are precisely $A_{\alpha(j)}\to Y_{\alpha(j)}$, all categorical equivalences. Steps 2-5 therefore apply in dimension $r$ to prove that $q_\sigma$ is a categorical equivalence. This includes noninjective $\alpha$; no fibrancy assumption on the $A_i$ has been introduced.

source.place: Remark 3.2.2.2 and the paragraph following Proposition 3.2.2.8: explicit mapping-simplex pullback formula and preservation of the quasi-equivalence hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-simplexwise-categorical-base-change] to $M(A)\xrightarrow{q}Y\xrightarrow{p}\Delta^n$. Step 6 verifies its hypothesis for every standard simplex over the base. It follows that $q_T$ is a categorical equivalence for every small $T\to\Delta^n$, with no restriction that $T$ be a quasicategory or that this map be injective. If $T$ is empty both pullbacks are empty. If $n=0$, the induction begins with the given fibre equivalence, and the same simplexwise argument still proves its product/base-change assertion; it is not inferred from unproved right properness. If some fibres are empty, the corresponding quantifications over their vertices and mapping-set pairs are empty and essential surjectivity on that region still follows from the given fibre equivalence. All constructions stay in a universe containing the given small simplicial sets.

source.place: Proposition 3.2.2.7(2), obtained from Proposition 3.2.2.8 and the dimension induction of Proposition 3.2.2.10.
